newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan considers floating oil-price system - paper.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan considers floating oil-price system - paper.

text.p: Taiwan monopoly Chinese Petroleum Corp may adopt a floating price system and lower its petroleum prices in July as world crude oil prices fall, local media reported on Tuesday.

The state-owned Chinese Petroleum is considering introducing a system whereby its petroleum prices would be adjusted weekly on the basis of import costs, rather than a few times a year as is currently done, the Commercial Times reported.
Chinese Petroleum executives could not be reached for immediate comment.
The newspaper said the floating-price system may begin as early as July, combined with a petroleum price reduction that would reflect Taiwan's falling crude import costs.
Chinese Petroleum's oil import costs averaged US$17.76 per barrel in May, down from $18.52 in April, company figures show.
The firm was expected to announce its earnings on June 10, with an accumulated budgetary deficit, sources said.
Chinese Petroleum has boosted local prices by about 12 percent in 1997, with an average nine percent increase on January 1 and a further 2.97 percent rise on April 4.
Executives said the added revenues were needed, despite a general decline in world crude prices, to cover an accumulated budgetary deficit for the fiscal year ended June 30.
